what: Insmed develops medicines for rare respiratory and inflammatory diseases. Its approved product Arikayce treats a chronic lung infection, and brensocatib has been approved for bronchiectasis, a chronic lung condition with no previous treatment.
customers: Pulmonologists, hospitals and health systems treating rare lung disease.
money: inhaled treatment for refractory lung infection
first treatment approved for non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis
moat: A first approved treatment for a condition affecting hundreds of thousands of people who previously had none, with patent protection and years of trial data behind it.
risks: It still makes a large operating loss while launching
Revenue depends almost entirely on how quickly brensocatib is adopted
It has raised money repeatedly and may need to again
The shares price in a very successful launch
opportunities: Revenue grew about 67% last year and about 35% a year over three years
Gross margin of 80% means scale would turn into profit quickly
Analysts see large upside, reflecting the size of the bronchiectasis market
watch: Brensocatib prescription uptake and the cash position.
